title: Complete two-pivot caller readers and certify fixed-chart retiming costs
body:
## Summary

- Complete both dirty-pivot readers and every original-input reader in the two-pivot caller. For n=2q+2, the all-q histogram is H_(2f)=n²+2, H_(4f)=1: full stock plus 8f.
- Certify the fixed six-bank native-product chart floor at 72f using 36 edge-disjoint odd Eulerian subgraphs, with a matching word. Complete eight-bank quadratic retimings improve 138f to 130f against stock 128f; they remain unfavorable.
- Add only `research/two-pivot-caller-readers/`. The [evidence index](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7/research/two-pivot-caller-readers/EVIDENCE-INDEX.md) maps every retained file to its verification role: 14 mathematical JSON dependencies, one status-only dependency, 12 archival mathematical receipts, and two attribution JSON files. All 59 retained files remain mandatory for the integrity gate. The original 277,041-line import was 98.4% JSON; this follow-up adds only the index and README link, preserving every frozen byte and pin.

## Scope and limits

The all-q construction covers integers q≥2 and f≥1. The 72f floor applies only to the retained six-bank skeleton and native-product chart compiler. It is not a bound for changed callers, new charts, or all eight-bank words. Finite exact replays and written all-parameter proofs are separate evidence.

The broader favorable-supplier target remains open: literal selected-native lowerings, contracting splits, compatible BIT, owners, precision, storage, fixed-tape costs and complete recursive/outer admission are unresolved. No new κ, selected-frontier change or formal-kernel theorem is claimed.

See the [proof](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7/research/two-pivot-caller-readers/FIXED-CHART-PROOF.md), [coverage and limits](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7/research/two-pivot-caller-readers/README.md), and [task, scope change and open next questions](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7/research/two-pivot-caller-readers/TASK.json).

## Test plan

- [x] At documentation head `6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7`, `python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/two-pivot-caller-readers --check-source-history` and `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-pivot-caller-readers --check-only` pass: committed bytes, source history, metadata and pins.
- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-pivot-caller-readers` passes both registered commands (normal and optimized Python) at that head.
- [x] Index links, complete 59-file binding coverage, category counts and byte/line totals checked against the retained inventory, static consumers and an observed direct replay. All 70 pre-existing package files other than README are byte- and mode-identical to `896e2a2e89fd2b54d4defafaef3b91bb4b33b493`; the verifier and BINDINGS are unchanged. Separate AI review checked the index's coverage distinctions, including status-only reads and imported helpers versus unexecuted audits.
- [x] [Automatic CI run 39324524356](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39324524356) completed successfully at documentation head `6ea9d3a06275225f0ef2bdc306618842f09bccf7`, including planning and registered package replay. The final workflow status, conclusion and source SHA were read back. No manual GitHub check rerun was requested.
- [x] The [original scoped AI review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4055#pullrequestreview-5571573806) checked the all-q derivation and independently rebuilt the fixed-chart graph/certificate and matching word maps at `896e2a2e89fd2b54d4defafaef3b91bb4b33b493`; those scientific files remain unchanged.

The earlier author-reported Git-free export checks are recorded in the [canonical finding](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3606#discussioncomment-19039338); export was not repeated for this documentation-only change. AI review and finite replay are not independent human or formal-kernel acceptance.
